title: Whole Biconcave Cell and Grana Cutaway Comparison Scene
description: One static teaching comparison arrangement, one scene and zero new independent models. The whole accepted chloroplast cutaway occupies the broad rear-left area of a low scene-only slab; the complete accepted biconcave erythrocyte sits separately toward the front-right. Both preserve their original enlarged illustrative metre dimensions, all meshes, oriented geometry and normal buffers, full constant PBR material dictionaries and complete internal hierarchy. Only whole-instance translations and one finite scene-only display slab are new. The free front strip and space between the two whole objects make their different exterior/cutaway representations readable without overlap. No cell, membrane, granum, lamella or rim is extracted, recoloured, resized or counted again. The two models use different illustrative enlargement factors; their displayed relative sizes are NOT a comparison of real biological dimensions. This is a general classroom juxtaposition of an animal-cell exterior and a plant-organelle diagram, not an erythrocyte containing chloroplasts, a single biological system, complete organelle anatomy, medical diagnosis, physiological process, working apparatus, load or stability certification. No labels, rig, animation or interaction made or claimed.
